summary.name: A New Bee's First Oncall
summary.one_liner: A blog post by Honeycomb developer advocate Liz Fong-Jones describing her first on-call week as a new engineer and what it taught her about production work and sustainable software development.
use_cases: Understanding how an engineering team runs on-call rotations
Learning how a small team handled a multi-node outage and a regression
Reading an example of reducing toil by upgrading infrastructure instead of automating a workaround
Seeing how continuous deployment supports quick reverts
Getting perspective on why a developer advocate joins on-call
summary.what_it_does: The post is a first-person account by Liz Fong-Jones, a new Honeycomb engineer and developer advocate, of her first on-call week. It describes two paging incidents: a simultaneous watchdog timeout of two redundant nodes serving one data shard, and a Friday regression where traces stopped loading for a customer. It also covers a series of non-urgent tickets caused by a Linux kernel memory management bug on Ubuntu 14.04, which the team fixed by upgrading to 18.04 rather than automating restarts. The author explains that deploying hourly makes reverting a bad commit easy, and that high-cardinality instrumentation helped confirm the scope of impact.
notable: First-hand account of a real on-call week with incident details
Explains why a developer advocate chose to join on-call
Describes choosing an OS upgrade over an automatic machine-restart script to remove toil
Notes hourly deploys made reverting regressions quick
caveats: Describes one week at one company (2018); practices may have changed since
Page is a blog post, not a tool documentation page, so it does not describe a product's full feature set
